THE SHANGHAI TRAMWAY STRIKE

(Taken from a report written by a
member of the Communist Party).

(Part V).

COMMENT ON THE STRIKE BY THE STANDING COMMITTEE OF THE
SHANGHAI GENERAL LABOUR UNION

The cause of the failure of the recent tramway strike is
largely attributable to the mistaken policy on the part of the
strike leaders who simply relied on individual terroristic
measures to maintain the strike, and paid little or no attention
to mass movement which should be the fundamental basis of a
strike. The leaders simply wasted the powerful and organized
force of the mass and insisted on terrorism to exercise their
control over the strikers. A programme of Red terrorism comes
into play before and after a strike in the event of the situation
assuming a grave aspect. The workers had no voice practically
and they remained out because they were afraid.

The General Labour Union did the right thing in ordering the
strike leaders to do away with terroristic measures, but they,
instead of taking it in good part, were rather inclined to doubt
the attitude of the union. Under the circumstances in which the
recent strike was conducted no worker would have thought of his
own power even if the strike had been successful because he
was simply following the command of despotic leaders. On Dec.
16 and 17 the management nearly succeeded in breaking the strike
for the simple reason that it lacked solidarity.

Some accuse the union for the failure of the strike because
it did not approve of the terroristic measures to be adopted
against motorman No. 195, but this is ridiculous. If we allow
the workers to indulge in such a serious crime we would have,
before long, incurred the enmity of the workers whose real
enemy is the capitalist. The reactionary elements would have
availed themselves of the opportunity to denounce the communists
page_data.zh:
(23)

上海電車罷工

（摘錄自一名共產黨員撰寫的報告）。

（第五部分）。

上海總工會常務委員會對罷工的評論

最近電車罷工失敗的原因，很大程度上歸咎於罷工領導人的錯誤政策，他們單純依靠個人的恐怖手段來維持罷工，而幾乎沒有關注作為罷工根本基礎的群眾運動。領導人只是浪費了強大且有組織的群眾力量，並堅持使用恐怖主義來行使對罷工工人的控制。在局勢變得嚴峻的情況下，紅色恐怖計劃在罷工前後發揮作用。工人們實際上沒有發言權，他們因為恐懼而繼續停工。

總工會命令罷工領導人放棄恐怖手段，這是正確的舉措，但他們非但沒有欣然接受，反而傾向於懷疑工會的態度。在最近這次罷工進行的情況下，即使罷工成功，也沒有工人會想到自己的力量，因為他們只是服從專制領導人的命令。12月16日和17日，資方幾乎成功破壞了罷工，原因很簡單，就是缺乏團結。

有些人指責工會導致罷工失敗，因為工會不贊成對195號電車司機採取恐怖手段，但這是很荒謬的。如果我們允許工人沉溺於如此嚴重的罪行，我們不久就會招致工人的敵意，而他們真正的敵人是資本家。反動分子會利用這個機會譴責共產黨人

page_data.en:
(24)
as murderers, incendiaries and what not. At the time the morale
of the strikers was on the wane and even if the murder of the
motorman had succeeded in prolonging the strike for a few days,
the hardships that they would have had to undergo during this
period would have estranged the relations between the strikers
and the leaders. Some think that the recent strike was a
complete failure but the strikers themselves, in fact, believe
that it helped them a great deal in the way of bettering their
conditions.
The recent strike of tramway employees taught us a valuable
lesson and has convinced us that wholesale terrorism based on
individual action is not only fatal to the labour movement but
also tends to injure the relations between the leaders and the
workers. This is where the necessity for a radical change in
the attitude of strike leaders comes in.
During the recent strike the leaders believed in the
omnipotence of terrorism, which they thought would enable them
to lead the workers to victory, and practically paid no attention
to a concerted movement of the strikers. The strike committee,
of course, was there but it simply existed in name. It never
met even once not to speak of holding formal meetings of repre-
sentatives. The committee consisted of several persons belong-
ing to the Municipal(?) General Labour Union and a number of
unemployed labourers who busied themselves a little just to
save their "face." None of the strikers were represented on
the committee and therefore they were hardly aware of its
existence. The union always took the lead when determining
the policy of the strikers. The majority of the communists
represented on the sub-committee were simply figure heads and
few of them took an active part in the strike campaign.
The Municipal(?) General Labour Union vainly employed a
number of agents with a view to establishing unity and solidarity
among the strikers.
During the strike the union was supplanted by the local
branch of the Communist Party. This was, however, a great
page_data.zh:
(24)
為謀殺犯、縱火犯等等。當時罷工者的士氣正在衰退，即使謀殺電車司機成功將罷工延長了幾天，他們在這段期間所遭受的艱難困苦也會疏遠罷工者與領導人之間的關係。有些人認為最近的罷工徹底失敗，但罷工者 themselves 實際上相信，這在改善他們的條件方面對他們有很大幫助。
最近的電車員工罷工給了我們一個寶貴的教訓，使我們確信，基於個人行動的大規模恐怖主義不僅對勞工運動是致命的，而且傾向於損害領導人與工人之間的關係。這就是罷工領導人態度需要徹底改變的原因所在。
在最近的罷工中，領導人相信恐怖主義的萬能，認為這能使他們帶領工人走向勝利，而實際上幾乎沒有關注罷工者的協調行動。罷工委員會當然存在，但它只是徒有虛名。它甚至從未開過一次會，更不用說舉行正式的代表會議了。委員會由幾名屬於市(?)總工會的人和一批失業勞工組成，他們稍微忙碌一下只是為了保住「面子」。罷工者在委員會中沒有代表，因此他們幾乎不知道委員會的存在。在確定罷工者的政策時，工會始終處於主導地位。在小組委員會中代表的共產黨人多數只是擺設，很少有人積極參與罷工運動。
市(?)總工會徒勞地僱傭了一批代理人，試圖在罷工者中建立團結和凝聚力。
在罷工期間，工會被共產黨地方支部所取代。然而，這是一個巨大的

page_data.en:
(25)

mistake for it caused the workers to forget the union and
at the same time to disregard the local branch of the Com-
munist Party as the centre of their activities. This is why
the strike failed as a mass movement. In view of this, we
should, in future, see to it that the union functions in-
dependently of the Communist Party.

Hitherto the Municipal(?) General Labour Union has limited
its activities to the tramway workers in the international
settlement only. This is a very bad policy so far as the
strike is concerned. Workers belonging to one particular
avocation can not successfully carry out a strike without help
from their comrades engaged in other occupations. The recent
strike was also an independent movement.

On December 12 when the strikers were at the height of
anxiety over the vigorous measures adopted by the company,
endeavours were made to induce the tramway and 'bus employees
to join the strike but without success.

The propaganda work was not quite satisfactory in most
cases. The strike bulletin containing strike intelligence and
our opinions and handbills dealing with various problems
occurring daily were distributed among the strikers but not
in a satisfactory manner. Many strikers never received a copy.

As regards the report on the strike, we regret to notice
that it contains no statistics, no details of the demands
and no report on the livelihood or calibre of the workers who
took part in the strike.

The Standing Committee of the Shanghai
General Labour Union.
(The end).

(Sent in March 21, 1928, 9.45 a.m.).
page_data.zh:
(25)

錯誤，因為這導致工人們忘記了工會，同時也不再把共產黨地方支部視為他們活動的中心。這就是罷工作為一場群眾運動失敗的原因。鑑於此，我們今後應確保工會獨立於共產黨運作。

迄今為止，市(?)總工會的活動僅限於國際租界內的電車工人。就罷工而言，這是一個非常糟糕的政策。從事某一特定職業的工人，如果沒有其他行業同志的幫助，無法成功進行罷工。最近的罷工也是一場獨立的運動。

12月12日，當罷工者因資方採取的強硬措施而處於極度焦慮之中時，曾試圖勸說電車和巴士員工加入罷工，但未獲成功。

宣傳工作在大多數情況下並不令人滿意。包含罷工情報和我們觀點的罷工簡報，以及處理每日發生各種問題的小冊子，雖然分發給了罷工者，但方式並不令人滿意。許多罷工者從未收到過一份。

關於罷工報告，我們遺憾地注意到，其中沒有統計數據，沒有訴求的細節，也沒有關於參加罷工工人的生計或素質的報告。

上海總工會常務委員會。
（完）。

（1928年3月21日上午9點45分送出）。

THE SHANGHAI TRAMWAY STRIKE

(Taken from a report written by a member
of the Communist Party).

(Part III).

December 13th passed without any noteworthy incidents.
On December 14th the strike situation still remained unchanged.
Our firm position gave no room for the company's running dogs
to enter and menace our citadel and it was then that the manage-
ment realized the futility of prolonging the strike. The
management eventually approached Wong Yuen Ching 王雲卿 who,
knowing that the strikers were waiting for the company to
suggest the opening of negotiations, consented to act as
mediator. Wong thereupon deputed a conductor to inform us
of his intention to interview our representatives and the
messenger brought a note containing the following conditions:-
    (1) That you appoint delegates to negotiate the settlement
of the strike with comprador Woo Tse Yu 胡子輿 , acting
on behalf of the management.
    (2) That a formal request to open negotiations be made to
the mediators by the Tramway Employees Club in order to
manifest its willingness to wind up the strike.
    A meeting was held by the local branch of the Communist
Party in connection with the foregoing matter when the
following recommendations were made:-
    (1) That a reply be given to the mediators to the effect
that our representatives will enter into negotiations for
a settlement with Wong Yuen Ching 王雲卿 , Li Ping 李斌 ,
Woo Tse Yu 胡子輿 and Nyi Ling Zai 倪廷瑞 , at a tea-shop
called Ih Loh Tien .
    (2) That a note urging the company to reply to our
demands within a specified period be sent to the management
at the same time hinting that we are willing to enter into
negotiations apart from these demands if necessary.
    (3) That a letter be addressed to Chiang Siao San warning
him not to work against the interests of the strikers and
page_data.zh:
(15)

上海電車罷工

（摘錄自一名共產黨員撰寫的報告）。

（第三部分）。

12月13日平靜度過，未發生任何值得注意的事件。12月14日，罷工局勢仍然沒有變化。我們堅定的立場讓資方的走狗無隙可乘，無法威脅我們的堡壘，這時資方意識到延長罷工是徒勞的。資方最終接觸了王雲卿 (Wong Yuen Ching)，他知道罷工者正等待資方提出開啟談判的建議，因此同意擔任調解人。王雲卿隨即派遣一名售票員告知我們他打算會見我們的代表，信使帶來了一張紙條，包含以下條件：
    (1) 你們委派代表與代表資方行事的買辦胡子輿 (Woo Tse Yu) 談判解決罷工事宜。
    (2) 電車員工俱樂部應向調解人提出開啟談判的正式請求，以表現其結束罷工的意願。
    共產黨地方支部就上述事項召開了一次會議，提出了以下建議：
    (1) 回覆調解人，表示我們的代表將與王雲卿 (Wong Yuen Ching)、李斌 (Li Ping)、胡子輿 (Woo Tse Yu) 和倪廷瑞 (Nyi Ling Zai) 在一家名為 Ih Loh Tien 的茶館進行解決問題的談判。
    (2) 同時向資方發送一封便箋，敦促其在規定期限內答覆我們的訴求，並暗示如有必要，我們願意在這些訴求之外進入談判。
    (3) 致信蔣小三 (Chiang Siao San)，警告他不要做損害罷工者利益的事，並

page_data.en:
(14)
attitude
speedily to change his mind and mediate towards the strike.
These three letters were despatched on December 14.
Consequent on the execution of our programme of terrorism,
many inspectors came to the club and pledged their loyalty
to our cause. They admitted their folly in having accepted
the orders of the management for the operation of a limited
number of cars as a demonstration against the strikers and
tendered their apologies in a most humble manner. All this
was due to the formidable position of the strikers.
as
December 16 came, day happened to be the pay day of the
conductors and motormen. In view of our failure in advising
the mechanics to go and get their pay which we thought might
help us to prolong the strike, this time we decided not to
allow any workers to receive their pay. It will be recalled
that it was on pay day that the management got hold of the
mechanics and tried to break the strike by means of counter-
propaganda. Explanations were given to the workers regarding
the inadvisability of going to the company to receive their
pay, but in vain. Their thirst for money was so strong that
it was impossible for us to prevail upon them over this
question. Uneasiness was fast developing among the men whose
relations with the club were gradually being alienated.
On December 15 further registration of 380 workers, 180
belonging to the new depot and 200 belonging to the old depot,
took place.
On this day we assembled all the point boys and discussed
about the question of forming a body of boy scouts. We found
it very difficult to deal with those workers who hail from
Kompo. They persisted in getting their pay and had no ears
for anything else. The strike was on the downward grade but
this mattered nothing to them. Three foreign and Chinese
Policemen raided the club at 2 p.m. and seized several kinds
of pamphlets and handbills issued by the Communist Party.
At the time no less than 50 inspectors were in conference.
The Police evidently suspected that we were engaged in unlawful
page_data.zh:
(14)
迅速改變主意，為罷工進行調解。
這三封信於12月14日發出。
由於執行了我們的恐怖主義計劃，許多督察來到俱樂部，宣誓效忠我們的事業。他們承認接受資方命令運營少量車輛以對抗罷工者是愚蠢之舉，並以極為謙卑的態度道歉。所有這一切都是因為罷工者強大的地位。
12月16日到來，那天恰逢售票員和司機的發薪日。鑑於我們此前勸告機械工去領取薪水失敗——我們原以為這可能有助於延長罷工——這次我們決定不允許任何工人領取薪水。回想起來，正是在發薪日，資方控制了機械工，並試圖通過反宣傳來破壞罷工。我們向工人解釋了去公司領薪水的不可取之處，但徒勞無功。他們對金錢的渴望如此強烈，以至於我們無法在這個問題上說服他們。工人中的不安情緒迅速蔓延，他們與俱樂部的關係逐漸疏遠。
12月15日，又有380名工人進行了登記，其中180人屬於新車庫，200人屬於舊車庫。
當天，我們召集了所有看道童（point boys），討論組建童子軍隊伍的問題。我們發現很難應對那些來自虹口 (Kompo) 的工人。他們堅持要領薪水，對其他事情充耳不聞。罷工雖已走下坡路，但這對他們來說無關緊要。下午2點，三名中外警察突襲了俱樂部，繳獲了共產黨發行的幾種小冊子和傳單。當時，不少於50名督察正在開會。警方顯然懷疑我們從事非法

page_data.en:
(15)

activities and that we had contraband on the premises.

(IV) Change in the Situation:
December 16 being the pay day of the conductors and motormen we sent out pickets to Soochow Road and its vicinity in order to prevent the workers from going to the Tramway Co.'s head office on Soochow Road. They kept watch from 8 a.m. to noon and again from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. All the workers went there in mufti but our vigilant agents succeeded in spotting 25 of them of whom 5 had already obtained their pay. Some of the workers who fell into the hands of our pickets were entirely ignorant of the orders issued by us prohibiting them to draw their wages.

On this day the offices of the company were filled with bags containing tickets and other necessary articles. This clearly shows that the management expected many workers turning up and intended to compel them to resume work.

At 2 p.m. on the same day our representatives met with Wong Yuen Ching, Li Ping, Nyi Ling Zai and Woo Tse Yu at the Ih Loh Tien tea-shop and handed them a letter from the club asking these four men to act as arbitrators on behalf of the labour union. All of them willingly gave their consent to the matter. Woo said that the party will hold a preliminary meeting with the management prior to entering into negotiations and the results of the meeting would be communicated to the strikers on the coming Monday. Woo was rather optimistic over the negotiations and stated that there was a possibility of all the demands submitted by the workers being accepted with the exception of that referring to recognition of the club. He assured us that no matter what the capitalists had to say he would see to it that due consideration was given to the workers' demands. "So far as the monetary question is concerned", said Woo, "You are not to worry about it: if the foreigners refuse to give in I have a way to solve it for you."

The negotiations promised us success and the morale of
page_data.zh:
(15)

活动，且我们处所内藏有违禁品。

（四）局势变化：
12月16日是售票员和司机的发薪日，我们派出纠察队前往苏州路及其附近地区，以阻止工人前往位于苏州路的电车公司总部。他们从上午8时至中午，以及下午2时至5时进行监视。所有工人均便衣前往，但我们警觉的探员成功辨认出其中25人，另有5人已领到薪水。部分落入我们纠察队手中的工人，完全不知晓我们发布的禁止他们领取工资的指令。

当天，公司办公室里堆满了装有车票及其他必需品的袋子。这清楚地表明，管理层预计会有许多工人前来，并打算强迫他们复工。

同日下午2时，我们的代表在“益乐天”茶馆与黄元清、李平、倪玲仔（音译）和吴子玉会面，并向他们递交了一封来自俱乐部的信函，请求这四名男子代表工会担任仲裁人。他们都欣然同意此事。吴氏表示，在与资方进入谈判之前，各方将举行一次预备会议，会议结果将于下周一告知罢工者。吴氏对谈判持相当乐观的态度，并称除了关于承认俱乐部这一项要求外，工人提出的所有要求都有可能被接受。他向我们保证，无论资本家怎么说，他都会确保工人的要求得到应有的考虑。“至于金钱问题，”吴氏说，“你们不必担心：如果洋人拒绝让步，我有办法为你们解决。”

谈判向我们预示着成功，而

page_data.en:
(16)

the strikers was on the wane. The Police raid on our club
on the 15th was, in the main, responsible for the unrest
amongst the strikers.

The report of the failure of the rising arrived from
Canton and this, coupled with the discovery of communistic
pamphlets, placards and handbills at the Tramway Employees
Club, greatly alarmed the capitalistic class in Shanghai
who suspected that the local communists were backing up the
tramway strike as a preliminary to a great Red uprising.
At 2 p.m. on December 16 a meeting was held at the club under
the auspices of the District Committee of the Communist Party
in celebration of the successful rising at Canton. The
majority of the strikers didn't know what it was all about
and consequently it met with little sympathy. When the
meeting was about to be called off, 2 foreign policemen and
8 or 9 Chinese constables again raided the club in company
with 2 foreign and Chinese detectives and destroyed all the
placards and posters on the wall and confiscated the desks,
chairs and other furniture. They drove the terrified strikers
out of the house at the point of their pistols.

Upon seeing that the club had been sealed by the Police,
a number of treacherous hands went to the company on Dec. 17
to get their pay. These men complained to the management
that the club was doing its best to prevent the strikers from
getting their wages. The matter was immediately reported to
the Police by the management and very soon detectives were
busily engaged in hunting for the pickets. Meanwhile all
kinds of rumours against us were being circulated amongst
the strikers and by 11 a.m. no fewer than 200 workers had
gone to receive their pay. The management then came to the
conclusion that the strikers were no longer under the control
of their leaders and availed itself of this opportunity to
win them over by counter-propaganda.

The management put all kinds of questions to the workers
on this day. They were asked: (1) You come here to get your
pay but you won't do any work? and (2) Why should the club
page_data.zh:
(16)

罢工者的士气却在衰退。警方于15日对我们俱乐部的突袭，主要是造成罢工者中间出现不安的原因。

广州起义失败的消息传来，加之在电车职工俱乐部发现了共产主义宣传册、标语和传单，这使上海的资本家阶级大为惊恐，他们怀疑当地共产党人正支持电车罢工，作为大规模红色起义的前奏。12月16日下午2时，在共产党区委会的主持下，俱乐部内举行了一次会议，以庆祝广州起义的成功。大多数罢工者并不知晓会议内容，因此并未获得多少同情。当会议即将解散时，两名外籍巡捕和八九名华捕再次会同两名中外侦探突袭了俱乐部，撕毁了墙上的所有标语和海报，并没收了桌椅及其他家具。他们用枪指着受惊的罢工者，将他们驱赶出屋。

看到俱乐部被警方查封后，12月17日，一些背叛者前往公司领取薪水。这些人向管理层抱怨，称俱乐部正竭力阻止罢工者领取工资。管理层立即将此情况报告给警方，很快侦探们便忙于搜捕纠察队员。与此同时，各种针对我们的谣言在罢工者中流传，到上午11时，已有不少于200名工人前去领薪。管理层随后得出结论，认为罢工者已不再受其领导人的控制，并利用这一机会通过反宣传来争取他们。

当天，管理层向工人提出了各种问题。他们被问道：（1）你们来这里领薪水，却不干活？以及（2）为什么俱乐部

page_data.en:
(17)

allow the mechanics to draw their pay and stop conductors
and motormen from doing so? The management told the workers
to report themselves at the depot on Monday when the attitude
of the company will be made known to them. The propaganda
of the management had a great effect on the minds of the
workers who soon began to voice their wrath against the club
without waiting to know what the management was going to do
about the matter. The general unrest was fast spreading even
amongst those who had refrained from getting their pay.

With the favourable turn in the situation caused by the
sealing of the club the management suddenly began to adopt
a very firm attitude towards the strikers. Wong Yuen Ching,
Li Ping, Nyi Ting Zai and Woo Tse Yu, who had promised to
play the part of arbitrators, quickly changed their attitude
and turned a deaf ear to the workers. Such being the case
the proposed negotiations for a settlement came to naught.

In view of this dramatic change in the situation which
considerably perturbed the strikers we came to the conclusion
that it would be futile for us to stop the strikers from
getting their pay any longer since many of them had already
received their money and had come to the following decisions:-

(2) That propaganda be carried out for an extended strike
campaign.
(1) That workers be permitted to receive their pay.
(3) That effective measures be taken to gain control over
the proletariat.
(4) That rigorous steps be adopted to punish the treacherous
workers.
(5) That a new Tramway Employees Club be organized.

These resolutions were put into effect on December 18
with the exception of No. 4. The second and third resolutions
of course will take time and we did all what we could but
this could not be regarded as satisfactory.

On December 18 we encouraged the strikers, as per our
decision on the previous day, to go and get their pay from
the company. The workers were rather hard up and they were
page_data.zh:
(17)

允许机务人员领取薪水，却阻止售票员和司机这样做？管理层告诉工人，周一到车厂报到，届时公司将向他们表明态度。管理层的宣传对工人的思想产生了巨大影响，工人们甚至不等知晓管理层将如何处理此事，便开始表达对俱乐部的愤怒。普遍的不安情绪迅速蔓延，甚至在那些尚未领薪的人中间也是如此。

随着俱乐部被封导致局势出现有利转折，管理层突然开始对罢工者采取非常强硬的态度。曾承诺担任仲裁人的黄元清、李平、倪廷仔（音译）和吴子玉迅速改变了态度，对工人的诉求充耳不闻。鉴于这种情况，拟议中的和解谈判化为泡影。

鉴于这一令罢工者深感不安的戏剧性局势变化，我们得出结论，继续阻止罢工者领薪已无意义，因为许多人已经拿到了钱，并做出了以下决定：

（2）开展宣传，进行延长罢工的斗争。
（1）允许工人领取薪水。
（3）采取有效措施以掌控无产阶级。
（4）采取严厉步骤惩罚背叛的工人。
（5）组建一个新的电车职工俱乐部。

除第4项外，这些决议于12月18日开始实施。第二和第三项决议自然需要时间，我们虽已尽力，但结果不能令人满意。

12月18日，根据前一天的决定，我们鼓励罢工者去公司领取薪水。工人们手头相当拮据，他们

page_data.en:
(18)
very pleased but at the same time they began to suspect our
position because of the sudden change in our attitude. The
strikers were now becoming weary of the struggle although
it was not so acute as to produce immediate results.
On December 19 the management issued a notice to the
strikers advising them to sever connection with the Communist
Party and to resume work immediately. They were also promised
a general increase of pay. This news was received by the
workers with great enthusiasm.
It so happened at this time that the Soviet Consular
Staff was driven away from Shanghai and this gave the management
every confidence that the strike would not now last very long.
It suspected that the Soviet government was at the back of
the movement.
(To be continued).
(Sent in March 17, 1928, 9.45 a.m.).
page_data.zh:
(18)
对此感到非常高兴，但同时也因我们态度的突然转变而开始怀疑我们的立场。罢工者现在对斗争感到厌倦，尽管这种厌倦尚未严重到产生直接后果的地步。
12月19日，管理层向罢工者发布通告，劝告他们切断与中国共产党的联系，并立即复工。他们还承诺普遍加薪。工人们热情高涨地接受了这一消息。
恰逢此时，苏联驻沪领事馆人员被驱逐出上海，这使得管理层深信罢工不会持续太久。他们怀疑苏联政府在幕后支持这场运动。
（待续）。
（1928年3月17日上午9时45分呈报）。

page_data.en:
(19)

THE SHANGHAI TRAMWAY STRIKE
(Taken from a report written by a
member of the Communist Party).

(Part IV)

(V) Dramatic Failure of the Strike:
The first 3 tramcars to be operated after the strike came
out from the old depot on December 20: they were led by one
driven by motorman No. 195. The sight of this demonstration
was too much for the strikers and the murder of the motorman
was strongly advocated by these men and the members of the
Communist Party. The officials of the General Labour Union,
however, held a different view, asserting that if the programme
of red terrorism is to be carried out at all it should not be
done individually but should be directed as a mass movement.
This argument was right: since the management suspected that the
strike was not a concerted movement it was up to the strikers to
disprove this. The relations between the General Labour Union
and our party was not quite as satisfactory as it ought to be
at that time and naturally we remained rather indifferent towards
its advice. We were thoroughly convinced that terrorism was
the only weapon with which to fight our way up and on December
20 we held a sub-committee meeting and a meeting of strikers
at the new and old depots respectively and pointed out that if
the strike is to continue the adoption of terroristic measures
was imperative and it was the only way to save the situation.
Upon hearing this the General Labour Union issued instructions
prohibiting the carrying out of the foregoing resolution.
The sub-committee met again on December 21 and in view of
the attitude of the General Labour Union and the lack of spirit
among the strikers it decided to call off the strike un-
conditionally on December 23. Four cars were in operation on
December 23.
On the morning of December 22 trouble arose among the
mechanics over the question of resumption of work. The foremen
were very much against unconditional resumption which they regarded
page_data.zh:
(19)

上海电车罢工
（摘自一名共产党员撰写的报告）。

（第四部分）

（五）罢工的戏剧性失败：
罢工后首批投入运营的三辆电车于12月20日从旧车厂开出：由195号司机驾驶的一辆车领头。这一示威景象让罢工者难以忍受，这些人及共产党员强烈主张谋杀该司机。然而，总工会官员持有不同观点，声称如果要实行红色恐怖计划，不应由个人单独行动，而应作为群众运动来指导。这一论点是正确的：既然管理层怀疑罢工并非协同行动，罢工者就有责任驳斥这一点。当时总工会与我们党的关系并不像应有的那样令人满意，因此我们自然对其建议相当冷漠。我们深信恐怖主义是我们突围的唯一武器，并于12月20日分别在新旧车厂召开了小组委员会会议和罢工者会议，指出如果要继续罢工，必须采取恐怖措施，这是挽救局势的唯一途径。听闻此言，总工会发布指令，禁止执行上述决议。
小组委员会于12月21日再次开会，鉴于总工会的态度以及罢工者缺乏斗志，决定于12月23日无条件取消罢工。12月23日有四辆电车在运营。
12月22日上午，机务人员在复工问题上发生纠纷。工头们强烈反对无条件复工，他们认为这

page_data.en:
(20)
as a great loss of "face". As the foremen were adamant the
conductors, motormen and the mechanics followed their example.
The sub-committee met for the last time at 1 p.m. on the
same day and unanimously passed a resolution calling for the
chastisement of motorman No. 195 at the hands of the Workers
Enemies Suppression Committee. The workers connected with this
committee were ordered to meet at the Tong Yu Tsung 全羽春 tea-
shop at 5 p.m. prior to embarking on their punitive expedition
as a demonstration against the company. The men were in high
spirits and great excitement also prevailed among the members of
the Communist Party. Two treacherous mechanics named Siao Woo
Zaung 小和尚 and Siao Moh Ziang 小木匠 came to know about the
plot and informed the Lauza Police. There were from 40 to 50
persons present at the teashop but all, except two, managed to
get away in time. A wholesale arrest would have been the result
had not the men learned of the approach of the Police in time.
The officials of the party barely managed to get away.
On December 23 the majority of the conductors and motormen
resumed work being encouraged by the fact that about 16 cars
were in operation on the previous day. On this day cars on
routes 1, 2, 6, 7, 8 and 9 were in operation and on December
24 even the railless cars resumed full service.
The mechanics thought that it was rather unwise for them to
resume work without any conditions and in order to ensure their
jobs they presented a demand to the management to the effect
that they will resume work on the condition that none of them
b be
are discharged. This was granted and all the mechanics went to
work on December 24 and thus the much-talked-about strike ended
in ignominious failure. After the resumption of work the
management petted and comforted the workers. The capitalist
declared that the ignorant workers had been exploited by the
Communist Party for its own sinister ends. The hands were
promised an extra annual bonus to cover the loss of pay caused
a
by the strike and in addition to this 8 per cent increase in pay.
The management expressed sympathy with the workers' demands
and there was no oppression, at least for the time being.
page_data.zh:
(20)
是极大的“丢面子”。由于工头们态度坚决，售票员、司机和机务人员也效仿他们的做法。
当天下午1时，小组委员会最后一次开会，一致通过决议，要求由工人敌人镇压委员会对195号司机进行惩处。与该委员会有关的工人奉命于下午5时在“全羽春”茶馆集合，随后出发进行惩罚性远征，以此作为对公司的示威。众人情绪高昂，共产党员中也弥漫着极大的兴奋情绪。两名名为小和尚和小木匠的背叛机务人员得知了这一阴谋，并向老闸捕房报案。茶馆内约有四五十人，但除两人外，其余人均及时逃脱。若非这些人及时获悉警方逼近，本会导致大规模逮捕。党的官员勉强得以脱身。
12月23日，大多数售票员和司机复工，前一天约有16辆电车在运营的事实鼓舞了他们。当天，1、2、6、7、8和9路电车恢复运营，12月24日甚至连无轨电车也恢复了全面服务。
机务人员认为无条件复工是不明智的，为了保住工作，他们向管理层提出一项要求，即在他们不被解雇的条件下复工。这一要求获准，所有机务人员于12月24日上班，至此，备受关注的罢工以可耻的失败告终。复工后，管理层对工人加以笼络和安抚。资本家宣称，无知的工人被中国共产党利用以达到其险恶目的。工人们被承诺发放额外的年终奖金，以弥补罢工造成的工资损失，此外还有8%的加薪。管理层对工人的要求表示同情，至少暂时没有出现压迫现象。

page_data.en:
(21)

The general feeling of the workers towards the Communist
Party, notwithstanding the failure of the strike, was very
satisfactory. They knew that the break-up was due to a number
of treacherous workers and we gave them no orders to resume
work. Although the strike itself cannot, by any means, be
called a success, the workers, nevertheless, learned one thing,
namely, wearisome as a strike always is, it yet it is a useful
weapon to better their conditions. Part of the demands were
realized through it.

The attitude of the strikers towards us and their views on
the strike, as depicted above, represent those of only a small
percentage of men, but I am convinced that they are not very
far from the truth.

Members of the Communist Party among the strikers were in-
active throughout the strike. These men, however, became rather
excited towards the end of the strike and demanded that the
party should authorize them to carry out terroristic measures
towards motorman No. 195 who was accused of treachery. We
could see no way of approving this individual movement and
insisted that whatever they did it must be based on concerted
action. This incurred their animosity. Our comrades at the
old depot and among the mechanics were comparatively easy to
manage and sub-committee meetings held by these men went on
very smoothly, but those belonging to the new depot were
ridiculously stubborn and failed to observe orders.

(VI) Conclusion:

In summing up the strike we now come to the conclusion
that it was not a concerted movement of workers started on
their own initiative. This was particularly true among the
conductors and the motormen.

It is hardly necessary for me to point out here that in
order to secure the leadership of the workers we must diffuse
among them the importance of the strike weapon. Of course our
actions must not be in any way influenced by their opinions.
But, in fact, we were hopelessly lacking in ability to agitate
page_data.zh:
(21)

尽管罢工失败，工人们对中国共产党的普遍好感仍令人满意。他们知道罢工的瓦解是由于少数工人的背叛所致，而我们并未下令让他们复工。虽然罢工本身无论如何都称不上成功，但工人们还是学到了一件事，即罢工虽然总是令人疲惫，但它仍是改善自身处境的有效武器。部分诉求正是通过罢工得以实现。

上述罢工者对我们的态度及其对罢工的看法，仅代表了极少数人的观点，但我确信这些观点与事实相去不远。

罢工者中的中国共产党成员在整个罢工期间一直不活跃。然而，这些人在罢工接近尾声时变得相当激动，并要求党授权他们对被指控背叛的195号电车司机采取恐怖手段。我们看不出批准这种个人行动的理由，并坚持认为无论他们做什么，都必须基于协同行动。这招致了他们的敌意。我们在旧车场以及机械工中的同志相对容易管理，这些人召开的小组委员会会议进行得非常顺利，但属于新车场的那些人则顽固得可笑，且不服从命令。

(VI) 结论：

综上所述，关于此次罢工，我们得出的结论是：这并非由工人自发发起的协同运动。在售票员和电车司机中情况尤其如此。

我在此无需指出，为了确立对工人的领导，我们必须向他们宣传罢工这一武器的重要性。当然，我们的行动绝不能受他们意见的任何影响。但事实上，我们在煽动

page_data.en:
(22)

the workers sufficiently to make them adopt a united front.
The strike was started at the instance of a minority of members of the Municipal General Labour Union and it lacked the sympathy and the support of the workers at large. Herein lies the chief cause of the failure of the strike. Part of the responsibilities, however, must be placed on the members of the local branch of the Communist Party who proved to be poor leaders so far as the strike was concerned.
As regards the question of stopping workers from receiving their pay, we now realize that it was an act of folly on our part. The strikers were facing acute hardships, with little hope for relief, and their pay was the only thing that could save them from this predicament.
It was indeed foolish of us to have resorted to force of arms when we could have successfully defended our positions by means of revolutionary propaganda work. We must meet propaganda with propaganda: no force is required here. We were so obsessed with the necessity of prolonging the strike that at times we disregarded the cries of the workers - cries that came from the innermost hearts of the men. This led to the alienation of the strikers which was speedily taken advantage of by the management.
It is an undeniable fact that the distribution of pamphlets, posters, handbills etc. in the club by some of the members of the district committee was a mistake and it brought about harmful results to the strike. In future we must see to it that the distinction between the party and labour bodies is upheld in all cases and everywhere. We also made a number of similar blunders during the strike; they are too numerous to mention.
We lost two of our valuable men in the Red Terror Party during the strike, spent an enormous sum of money and many of our comrades are groaning in prison cells.
It is truly a regrettable affair that the strike failed despite all that we had done.
(To be continued).
(Sent in March 20, 1928, at 9.45 a.m.)
page_data.zh:
(22)

工人方面能力严重不足，无法使他们采取统一战线。罢工是由市总工会（Municipal General Labour Union）少数成员发起的，缺乏广大工人的同情和支持。这正是罢工失败的主要原因。然而，部分责任必须归咎于中国共产党地方支部的成员，事实证明他们在罢工方面的领导能力很差。

关于阻止工人领取工资的问题，我们现在意识到这是我们愚蠢之举。罢工者面临严峻的困境，几乎没有获得救济的希望，而工资是唯一能让他们摆脱这种困境的东西。

当我们本可以通过革命宣传工作成功捍卫我们的立场时，却诉诸武力，这确实是愚蠢的。我们必须以宣传对抗宣传：此处无需使用武力。我们过于执着于延长罢工的必要性，以至于有时忽视了工人的呼声——那些发自工人们内心深处的呼声。这导致了罢工者的疏离，而资方迅速利用了这一点。

不可否认的事实是，区委员会的一些成员在俱乐部散发传单、海报、单页等是一个错误，给罢工带来了有害的后果。今后，我们必须确保在任何情况下、任何地方都保持党组织与劳工团体之间的区别。我们在罢工期间还犯了许多类似的错误；其数量之多，不胜枚举。

我们在红色恐怖党（Red Terror Party）中损失了两名宝贵的人员，花费了巨额资金，许多同志正在监狱牢房中受苦呻吟。

尽管我们做了一切努力，罢工仍然失败，这确实是一件令人遗憾的事情。
（待续）。
（1928年3月20日上午9时45分发出）

TRANSLATION OF EXTRACTS FROM NAIGAI WATA MILL INTELLIGENCE
REPORT

Strictly Confidential

The following is the full text of a report drafted by a
communist who had taken a leading part in the recent tramway
strike which lasted from November 28, 1927 to December 23,
1927 together with comments on same by the leaders.

During the strike wholesale terrorism was the order of the
day and the entire community was considerably alarmed at the
horrible measures adopted by the strikers and the communists
in order to prolong the struggle. These documents will
initiate us into the true facts of the conditions which pre-
vailed among the strikers at the time and in view of the
important bearing this will have on our strike policy, they
are published herewith for the information of the mill staff:-

Report follows:-

REPORT ON THE TRAMWAY STRIKE IN THE INTERNATIONAL
SETTLEMENT

The strike of tramway employees in the International
Settlement originated on November 28, 1927 and lasted up to
December 23, 1927. The strike was eventually frustrated and
all the employees resumed work unconditionally after being
absent from work for 26 days.

The report on the progress of the strike is given hereunder:-

(I) The Origin of the Strike:

The origin of the strike movement may be traceable to the
death of motorman No. 90 who was struck by a stray bullet
fired by a constable and the injuries sustained by another
motorman No. 8 who lost his fingers whilst on duty. In both
cases management failed to issue sufficient compassionate
grants and this aroused considerable public indignation.
Meanwhile the Municipal(?) General Labour Union lost no time
in propagating the incident on an extensive scale which
eventually culminated in a strike.

The first representative meeting of tramway employees was

绝密

以下是一名在最近一次从1927年11月28日持续至1927年12月23日的电车罢工中起主导作用的共产党员起草的报告全文，以及领导人对此报告的评论。

在罢工期间，大规模恐怖活动成为常态，罢工者和共产党人为延长斗争所采取的可怕措施使整个社区感到相当恐慌。这些文件将使我们了解当时罢工者中流行的真实情况，鉴于这对我们的罢工政策具有重要影响，现将其公布以供纱厂职员参考：-

报告如下：-

关于国际租界电车罢工的报告

国际租界电车员工的罢工始于1927年11月28日，持续至1927年12月23日。罢工最终受挫，所有员工在缺勤26天后无条件复工。

罢工进展情况报告如下：-

(I) 罢工的起源：

罢工运动的起因可追溯至90号电车司机的死亡，他被一名巡捕发射的流弹击中，以及另一名8号电车司机在执勤时受伤失去手指。在这两起事件中，管理层未能发放足够的抚恤金，这引起了公众相当大的愤慨。与此同时，市(?)总工会不失时机地大规模宣传这一事件，最终导致罢工爆发。

第一次电车员工代表会议于

page_data.en:
(2)

convened on November 17. Prior to this officers of our
branch here met on several occasions in which the question
of demands to be submitted to the management was agreed upon.
Several minor meetings were also held from time to time when
efforts were made to agitate the mass by means of explanations
regarding the cause of the strike.

It was at the meeting held on November 17 that the 17
demands were unanimously adopted. Before the meeting terminated
foreign and Chinese Police officers in mufti arrived at the
scene and dispersed the crowd. At the time there were a
large number of mechanics present at the meeting but the
number of conductors and motormen was comparatively small
because most of them were still on their way.

As a result of this first attempt made by the authorities
to curb our movements, on November 19, we submitted the
demands in question to the management of the Tramway Co. in
the name of the Tramway Employees Club, giving the time limit
of 3 days. In the meantime we did our utmost to encourage
the workers to remain firm and to struggle for their cause.
Three days passed but no reply was forthcoming and therefore
we decided to hold a meeting on November 23. However, on
the morning of this day the Police raided the club and later
posted constables on the premises thus preventing us from
holding the meeting. The attention of the Police was first
attracted to this club at the time of the mill strike in the
eastern district when millhands used the place as their
rendezvous.

It appears that the Police condemned the idea of provoking
the antipathy of the tramway workers by adopting too vigorous
measures towards them and it was this that prevented them
from doing anything beyond dispersing the crowd and preventing
us from holding the meeting.

The assassination of three detectives occurred on Nov.
22 and this was one of the causes why the Police began to
pay such a serious attention to the Tramway Employees Club.
Apparently they believed that members of the club had something
page_data.zh:
(2)

11月17日召开。在此之前，我们这里的支部官员多次开会，商定了向管理层提交的诉求事项。期间还不时举行几次小型会议，试图通过解释罢工原因来煽动群众。

正是在11月17日的会议上，17项诉求获得一致通过。会议结束前，便衣的外国和中国警察官员到达现场并驱散了人群。当时有大量机械工出席会议，但售票员和电车司机的人数相对较少，因为大多数人还在路上。

由于当局首次试图遏制我们的行动，我们在11月19日以电车员工俱乐部的名义向电车公司管理层提交了相关诉求，并给出了3天的期限。同时，我们竭尽全力鼓励工人保持坚定，为他们的事业而斗争。三天过去了，但没有得到任何回复，因此我们决定在11月23日举行会议。然而，当天早上警察突袭了俱乐部，随后在场所内部署了巡捕，从而阻止我们举行会议。警察首次注意到这个俱乐部是在东区纱厂罢工期间，当时纱厂工人将该地作为集合点。

看来，警察认为通过对电车工人采取过于严厉的措施来激起他们的反感是不可取的，这也正是防止他们采取除驱散人群和阻止我们开会以外的任何行动的原因。

11月22日发生了三名侦探被刺杀的事件，这是警察开始如此严肃关注电车员工俱乐部的原因之一。显然，他们认为俱乐部成员与此事有关

page_data.en:
(3)

to do with the assassination. At any rate, the raid of the
club was a serious blow to us. We lost our meeting place
and consequently our movements were considerably hampered.
The workers were panic-stricken and knew not what to do.
This was indeed a trying period for us all and we lost no
time in adopting emergency measures to cope with the situation.
Several persons were chosen from amongst the workers and
deputed to call on the management with a petition issued in
the name of the club. On the other hand, we forced two of
the leading employees of the company named Wong Yung Ching
王雲卿 and Li Ping 李斌 to use their influence with a
view to persuading the management into accepting the demands.
Needless to say we were ready to make a certain amount of
concessions provided that the management gave us a fair and
square deal. Nevertheless, on the other hand, every pre-
paration was made for the worst. Meetings were held under
all manner of pretexts and we urged all those present to
rise with one accord in the event of the declaration of a
strike which we knew was drawing near. In addition to this
we eliminated the dubious members in order to establish a
firm and formidable stand which will withstand the strike.
Despite all that we had done we could not deny one thing,
namely, the lack of sufficient influence on our part to
control the workers. The efforts on the part of the local
branch of the Communist Party brought little result, and the
officials of the organization department of the Municipal(?)
General Labour Union were also greatly discouraged and
showed little interest in the movement. The workers, to our
surprise, were not very much impressed by the demands, hence
the lack of concerted action and an unshakable stand.

(II) Declaration of the Strike:
The management of the Tramway Co. not only turned a deaf
ear to our demands and failed to give any reply even after
November 23, the expiry of our ultimatum, but it even went
so far as to induce the Provisional Court to issue an order
page_data.zh:
(3)

系。无论如何，对俱乐部的突袭对我们来说是一个沉重的打击。我们失去了集会地点，因此我们的行动受到了相当大的阻碍。工人们惊慌失措，不知所措。这对我们所有人来说确实是一段艰难的时期，我们立即采取紧急措施以应对局势。我们从工人中挑选了几个人，委派他们以俱乐部的名义递交请愿书拜访管理层。另一方面，我们迫使两名公司主要员工王雲卿和李斌利用他们的影响力，试图说服管理层接受诉求。不用说，只要管理层公平对待我们，我们准备做出一定的让步。尽管如此，另一方面，我们也为最坏的情况做好了准备。我们以各种借口举行会议，并敦促所有在场的人在宣布罢工（我们知道这已迫在眉睫）时团结一致行动起来。此外，我们还清除了可疑分子，以建立坚定且强大的立场，以经受住罢工的考验。尽管我们做了一切努力，但我们不能否认一件事，即我们缺乏足够的影响力来控制工人。中国共产党地方支部的努力收效甚微，市(?)总工会组织部的官员也大为气馁，对该运动表现出很少的兴趣。令我们惊讶的是，工人们对这些诉求印象并不深刻，因此缺乏协同行动和不可动摇的立场。

(II) 宣布罢工：
电车公司管理层不仅对我们的诉求充耳不闻，甚至在11月23日最后通牒期满后仍未给予任何答复，甚至进而促使临时法院发布命令

page_data.en:
(4)

for the sealing of the Tramway Employees Club which was
eventually carried out on the afternoon of November 25. As
a last measure, negotiations were carried out by us with the
company on November 26 and 27 through the medium of Wong Yung
Ching 王雲卿 and Li Ping 李斌 , two leading members of
the staff of the company, and a foreman named Wong Ah Foh
王阿福 but in vain. The rupture came about at 10 a.m. on
November 28 and as a result of this over 300 workers laid
down their tools and went on strike two hours after the
negotiations had been broken off. Considerable excitement
and animated feeling prevailed among the workers at this time
but unfortunately their movement lacked unity and control,
due chiefly to the fact that the majority of them were un-
aware of the true cause of the strike. We acted according
to circumstances and changed our policy accordingly.

Our chief aim was to secure the cancellation of the
sealing order of the club and on this condition we were pre-
pared to resume work but at the same time reserving to our-
selves the right to negotiate the demands submitted by us
to the management. On the other hand, however, preparations
were made in case of a rupture in the negotiations. Plans
had been afoot in our Party to organize a special committee
to control all the campaigns and the strike committee but,
after all, these plans did not eventuate.

The situation became somewhat grave on November 29, the
second day of the strike, and the company was eventually
compelled to curtail the service by one-third. None of the
workers who are members of the Communist Party reported for
duty that day and the strike situation grew more and more
tense. Later we met with the strikers at the Dong Yu Chun
全羽春 , a Chinese tea-shop, and pacified them in their
uneasiness and the possible failure of the strike. Another
meeting attended by more than 60 conductors and motormen was
held at a Chinese tea-shop called Ching Lien Koh 青蓮閣 .
A general feeling of anxiety prevailed amongst all the workers
at this time.
page_data.zh:
(4)

关于查封电车员工俱乐部一事，该行动最终于11月25日下午执行。作为最后手段，我们于11月26日和27日通过该公司两名主要职员王雲卿（Wong Yung Ching）和李斌（Li Ping），以及一名名叫王阿福（Wong Ah Foh）的工头与公司进行谈判，但徒劳无功。决裂发生于11月28日上午10时，因此在谈判破裂两小时后，300多名工人放下工具，举行罢工。此时工人群情激愤，情绪高涨，但不幸的是，他们的运动缺乏统一和控制，这主要是因为大多数人并不了解罢工的真正原因。我们根据情况行事，并相应地改变了策略。

我们的主要目标是争取取消对俱乐部的查封令，在此条件下我们准备复工，但同时保留我们就向管理层提出的要求进行谈判的权利。另一方面，我们也为谈判破裂做好了准备。我们党内部曾计划组织一个特别委员会来控制所有运动和罢工委员会，但毕竟这些计划并未实现。

11月29日，即罢工第二天，局势变得有些严峻，公司最终被迫将服务缩减三分之一。当天，身为共产党员的工人均未报到上班，罢工局势日益紧张。后来，我们在一家名为全羽春（Dong Yu Chun）的中式茶馆与罢工者会面，安抚了他们因不安及担心罢工可能失败而产生的情绪。另一次会议在一家名为青蓮閣（Ching Lien Koh）的中式茶馆举行，有60多名售票员和司机参加。此时所有工人中普遍存在着焦虑情绪。

page_data.en:
(5)

November 29 came but no word was heard regarding the
results of the negotiations we were carrying on with the
management through the foreman and the two leading employees.
These men, who were supposed to have been acting as a go-
between, xxxxxx avoided seeing us and failed to show up even
at the appointed time.

On November 30 practically the same number of cars were
running as the previous day but the strike atmosphere was fast
spreading amongst the motormen and conductors. The situation
presented such a grave aspect that the management knew that
within a few days the tramway service will have to be suspended
completely.

The mechanics on strike were highly indignant at the
indifference of the motormen and conductors in joining the strike
and a group of night shift mechanics attached to the Wayside
depot, numbering over 20, met at 8 a.m. on November 30 when they
decided to appeal to the Tramway Employees Club to issue an
order to all motormen and conductors to join the strike im-
mediately and to take the necessary steps to deal with traitors
and enemies. They threatened to resume work if no results
were forthcoming. These mechanics who are the followers of a
foreman named Li Min Chang 李鳴章 are in fact reactionaries;
their idea of presenting various demands to the club and other
organs in charge of the strike was to embarrass us rather
than to promote the strike. Therefore in dealing with them we
always bore this in our mind lest we be imposed upon by them.

In the meantime, in order to alleviate the situation which
was in no way sound at that time we passed the following
resolutions:-

(1) That orders be issued to all tramway workers to go on
strike immediately.

(2) That senior clerks and foremen be asked to act as
mediators.

(3) That a house be rented to be used as strike headquarters
and a meeting place.

(4) That steps be taken to impress on the minds of the
page_data.zh:
(5)

11月29日过去了，但关于我们通过工头和两名主要员工与管理层进行的谈判结果，未听到任何消息。这些本应充当中间人的人，xxxxxx 回避见我们，甚至在约定时间也未露面。

11月30日，运行的电车数量实际上与前一天相同，但罢工气氛正在司机和售票员中迅速蔓延。局势呈现出如此严峻的局面，以至于管理层知道在几天内电车服务将不得不完全停止。

罢工中的机械师对司机和售票员在加入罢工方面的冷漠态度感到极为愤怒，附属路边车场（Wayside depot）的一个夜班机械师小组，人数超过20人，于11月30日上午8时集会，当时他们决定呼吁电车员工俱乐部发布命令，要求所有司机和售票员立即加入罢工，并采取必要措施对付叛徒和敌人。他们威胁说，如果没有结果，他们将恢复工作。这些机械师是一名名叫李鳴章（Li Min Chang）的工头的追随者，实际上是反动分子；他们向俱乐部和其他负责罢工的机构提出各种要求的想法，是为了让我们难堪，而不是为了促进罢工。因此，在对付他们时，我们始终牢记这一点，以免被他们蒙骗。

与此同时，为了缓解当时绝不健康的局势，我们通过了以下决议：-

(1) 命令所有电车工人立即罢工。

(2) 请高级职员和工头担任调解人。

(3) 租赁一所房屋用作罢工总部和集会地点。

(4) 采取措施使

page_data.en:
(6)
strike the true cause and significance of the strike.
(5) That all available means be taken to exaggerate the impending strike of motormen and conductors so that it will bring about favourable results for the mechanics in their struggle against the company.
Our intention regarding the resolution No. 5 was to induce the company to arrive at a settlement in connection with the strike of mechanics before the strike spreads to the motormen and conductors because we were conscious of the fact that further development of the strike would bring havoc upon us.
The day passed but the situation still remained unchanged: we were finally compelled to issue an order for a general strike of tramway workers to take effect from the following day, December 1. On December 1 strike pickets were despatched in all directions to prevent workers from reporting for duty. The intimidation had a salutary effect but, nevertheless, a small number of men managed to evade the pickets and went to work. On this day in all 16 cars, 8 from the old depot and the same number from the new depot, were running. Upon seeing this the strikers became infuriated and a throng of them went to the club demanding an explanation. Since things had come to this pass we had no alternative but to organize a forlorn hope party to carry out our programme of red terrorism. Preparations were completed by 10 a.m.: and soon afterwards the party went out and attacked a tramcar running along Seward Road near the junction of Kungping Road. Our men fired at the car which was in motion and wounded two detectives and three passengers. Unfortunately two of our men were killed in this encounter. All cars stopped in the afternoon and our object was attained. Handbills were disseminated by us far and wide.

(III) Result of the General Tramway Strike:
All the mechanics, motormen and conductors having gone on strike from December 1, the management undertook to operate a limited number of cars on routes 2, 8 and 9 with
page_data.zh:
(6)
罢工者铭记罢工的真正原因和意义。
(5) 采取一切可用手段夸大司机和售票员即将发生的罢工，以便为机械师在与公司的斗争中带来有利的结果。
我们关于第5号决议的意图是，促使公司在罢工蔓延到司机和售票员之前，就机械师的罢工达成和解，因为我们意识到罢工的进一步发展会给我们带来灾难。
一天过去了，但局势仍然没有改变：我们最终被迫发布命令，电车工人的总罢工从次日12月1日起生效。12月1日，罢工纠察队被派往各处，以防止工人报到上班。这种恐吓产生了有益的效果，尽管如此，仍有少数人设法避开纠察队去上班。这一天总共有16辆电车运行，其中8辆来自旧车场，同样数量的8辆来自新车场。看到这种情况，罢工者变得愤怒起来，一大群人涌向俱乐部要求解释。既然事情已经发展到这一步，我们别无选择，只能组织一支敢死队来执行我们的红色恐怖计划。准备工作在上午10时完成：不久之后，该队出动，攻击了一辆行驶在塞华德路（Seward Road）靠近公平路（Kungping Road）交叉口附近的电车。我的人向行驶中的电车开火，打伤了两名侦探和三名乘客。不幸的是，我们的人在本次交火中有两人死亡。下午所有电车停运，我们的目标得以实现。我们四处散发传单。

(III) 电车总罢工的结果：
由于所有机械师、司机和售票员自12月1日起罢工，管理层承诺在

MILL DAILY INTELLIGENCE REPORT

Issued by the Intelligence Section.

THE SHANGHAI TRAMWAY STRIKE
(Taken from a report written by a
member of the Communist Party).
(Part II)

The manager of the Shanghai Tramway Co. was somewhat taken
by surprise to see the inspectors belonging to the old depot go
on strike on the morning of December 5 in sympathy with other
strikers and hurriedly deputed 5 inspectors to the Tramway
Employees Club to negotiate the settlement of the strike.
At this time our position was rather shaky owing to lack of
unity in the ranks of the striking workers and therefore we lost
no time in endorsing the manager's offer and accordingly sub-
mitted the following 4 demands as the primary conditions for
resumption of work:-
(1) That the Tramway Employees Club be reopened and the
company authorize the issue of $400 for the inauguration expenses
and a monthly subsidy of $200 as maintenance fund.
(2) That the family of the motorman No. 90 be given a
compassionate grant of $5,000.
(3) That all workers dismissed after the "May 30 incident"
in connection with movements connected with labour unions be
reinstated unconditionally.
(4) That all workers be given full pay for the strike period.
The management promised to give us a reply by the after-
noon of December 6, but upon seeing some motormen and conductors
reporting for duty on the afternoon of December 5, which
apparently gave the impression that the strike was lacking in
solidarity, it purposely held up the reply without giving any
definite reasons.
At this stage the morale of the strikers was in a precarious
state. On the morning of December 7 more than a hundred workers

纱厂每日情报报告

由情报科发布。

上海电车罢工
（摘自一名共产党员撰写的报告）。
（第二部分）

上海电车公司经理看到旧车场的稽查员于12月5日上午出于同情其他罢工者而举行罢工，感到有些意外，并急忙委派5名稽查员前往电车员工俱乐部，谈判解决罢工事宜。
此时，由于罢工工人队伍缺乏团结，我们的地位相当不稳，因此我们不失时机地认可了经理的提议，并相应地提交了以下4项要求作为复工的首要条件：-
(1) 重新开放电车员工俱乐部，公司授权拨付400元作为启动费用，每月补贴200元作为维持基金。
(2) 给予90号司机的家属5,000元抚恤金。
(3) 无条件复职在“五卅惨案”后因与工会运动有关而被解雇的所有工人。
(4) 所有工人在罢工期间获得全额工资。
管理层承诺在12月6日下午给我们答复，但在12月5日下午看到一些司机和售票员报到上班，这显然给人留下罢工缺乏团结的印象，因此它故意扣留答复，未给出任何明确理由。
在此阶段，罢工者的士气处于危险状态。12月7日上午，一百多名工人

page_data.en:
(9)

reported for duty and no less than 20 cars were in operation.
However, on the afternoon of the same day the service was
suspended completely owing to the attack on a Korean inspector
named Tsa Shing Feng 崔昇風 who received almost fatal injuries.
The intelligence on the part of the management regarding
the real character of the strike was somewhat lacking and con-
sequently it did nothing beyond oppressing the workers. Its
idea of operating cars in the face of imminent danger was also
meant as demonstration. No doubt at times the workers were
thrown into consternation through the forcible measures adopted
by the company, but on the other hand, it aroused considerable
indignation amongst the men. The mechanics, who were the
first to go on strike, were considerably enraged at the in-
activity of the officials of the club who would not dare to take
steps to prevent the workers from resuming. The attempt on the
life of a Korean inspector saved the "face" of the club con-
siderably because all the workers there and then decided to
remain out and did so. The strike was spreading among the
conductors and motormen but on the other hand it was on the wane
as far as the mechanics were concerned.
As December 7 was pay day, we told the mechanics to go to
the company and get their pay. We decided on this point because
we thought that the wages would help us to prolong the strike.
However, contrary to our expectations, the management availed
itself of the opportunity to spread counter-propaganda among
the hands, pointing out the futility of the strike and urging
them to resume work. The management expressed its willingness
to enter into negotiations for a settlement of the strike and
asked the workers to submit demands drafted by themselves. This
soon won over the treacherous workers who immediately drew up
the following 4 demands:-
(1) That recognition be given to the Tramway Employees Club.
(2) That wages be increased by 50 per cent.
(3) That a month's pay be given to each worker at the end
of each year as annual bonus.
page_data.zh:
(9)

报到上班，不少于20辆电车投入运营。然而，同日下午，由于一名名叫崔昇風（Tsa Shing Feng）的朝鲜籍稽查员遭到袭击并受致命重伤，服务完全停止。
管理层对罢工真实性质的情报 somewhat 缺乏，因此除了压迫工人外无所作为。它在迫在眉睫的危险面前运营电车的想法也是一种示威。毫无疑问，有时工人因公司采取的强制措施而感到惊恐，但另一方面，这在工人中引起了相当大的愤慨。最先罢工的机械师对俱乐部官员的不作为感到相当愤怒，因为这些官员不敢采取措施阻止工人复工。对一名朝鲜籍稽查员的暗杀企图在很大程度上挽回了俱乐部的“面子”，因为所有工人当即决定继续罢工，并确实这样做了。罢工正在售票员和司机中蔓延，但另一方面，就机械师而言，罢工势头正在减弱。
由于12月7日是发薪日，我们告诉机械师去公司领取工资。我们决定这一点是因为我们认为工资将有助于我们延长罢工。然而，与我们的预期相反，管理层利用这一机会在工人中散布反宣传，指出罢工的徒劳，并敦促他们复工。管理层表示愿意就解决罢工进行谈判，并要求工人提交自行起草的要求。这很快赢得了那些奸诈工人的支持，他们立即拟定了以下4项要求：-
(1) 承认电车员工俱乐部。
(2) 工资增加50%。
(3) 每年年底发给每位工人一个月的工资作为年终奖金。

page_data.en:
(10)

(4) That full pay be issued to workers for the strike
period.

The fact that the workers even went so far as to ignore
the existence of the club and to enter into direct negotiations
with the management goes to show the split in the ranks of
the strikers and the general depression in morale. This is
a vital blow to any strike.

The 4 demands were eventually rejected by the management
who by this time were fully aware of the lack of unity among
the strikers. The company issued a notice to the strikers
advising them to resume work by December 9 otherwise they
would all be dismissed. The management did everything in its
power to break the strike by inducing the strikers to resume
work but thanks to our tactful handling of the situation all
of them were unmoved.

In the meantime we rented a house to be used as the
Tramway Employees Club and succeeded in carrying out our
campaign. At that time, for some reason or other the Police
were not inclined to be too inquisitive about us and every-
thing went on very smoothly. It was rather difficult for us
to hold large meetings at this new club for it would attract
the attention of outsiders but minor meetings were held
almost every day.

In order to prevent the management from winning over
the minds of the strikers we did everything possible to
exercise full control over the workers. On December 8 we our
highly effective anti-capitalist propaganda pointed out
how they are exploiting the traitors in our ranks in order
to break the strike. On December 9, the day set by the
management for the men to resume work unconditionally, we
sent out pickets to prevent this. Furthermore, on the
following day in order to preserve order amongst the strikers
we issued instructions prohibiting extortion. It was on
this day that inspector No. 11 named Van Wei Tung 范偉東 was
assassinated.
page_data.zh:
(10)

(4) 向工人发放罢工期间的全额工资。

工人们甚至无视俱乐部的存在，直接与管理层进行谈判，这一事实表明了罢工者队伍内部的分裂以及士气的普遍低落。这对任何罢工来说都是致命的一击。

这四项要求最终被管理层拒绝，此时他们已充分意识到罢工者缺乏团结。公司向罢工者发出通知，劝告他们在12月9日前复工，否则将全部予以解雇。管理层竭尽全力，通过诱导罢工者复工来破坏罢工，但得益于我们对局势的巧妙处理，所有人都未为所动。

与此同时，我们租用了一处房屋作为电车员工俱乐部，并成功开展了我们的活动。当时，出于某种原因，警方不太倾向于对我们过于深究，因此一切进展都非常顺利。在这个新俱乐部举行大型集会对我们来说相当困难，因为这会吸引外人的注意，但小型会议几乎每天都在举行。

为了防止管理层争取罢工者的民心，我们尽一切可能对工人实行全面控制。12月8日，我们通过极具成效的反资本主义宣传，指出他们如何利用我们队伍中的叛徒来破坏罢工。12月9日是管理层规定的无条件复工之日，我们派出纠察队以防止此事发生。此外，次日为了维持罢工者内部的秩序，我们发布了禁止勒索的指令。正是在这一天，编号为11号的巡捕范伟东（Van Wei Tung）遇刺身亡。

page_data.en:
(11)

Representatives of workers belonging to the old depot
held a meeting on December 11 and urged the strikers to remain
firm and to fight to the last ditch. One of the speakers
declared, "If the foreign devils are going to declare a
holiday for a week we would remain out for another ten days."
As a result of this meeting a registration committee was
formed to control the movement. Strikers were assured of
strike relief funds and were told not to worry about the
strike. Cries of "Down with Chiang Siao San 蔣 少 山 , the
traitor," was clamorously voiced everywhere. Chiang is the
man who was chiefly responsible for the disorganization of
the strike. Our methods of controlling the strikers gradually
had salutary effect and the general indications at this time
were in our favour.

The proposed registration committee was still in course
of formation on December 12 when a registration office was
established. The inauguration of this office was a great
success. On this day alone no fewer than 800 workers were
registered with the office. Later house-to-house calls
were made and we were wide awake to make full use of our
calls. They were initiated into the real significance of
the struggle and were urged to remain unshaken.

Our aims at this stage of the strike were based on the
following three points:-

(1) To make use of the registration system to carry out
propaganda amongst the strikers.

(2) To carry out demonstrations against the company by
obtaining permission from the Shanghai Municipal Council.

(3) To establish a strike committee composed of 21
persons, 8 workers each from the old and new depots and 5
representing the mechanics.

On the same day we received a letter from the standing
committee of the Shanghai General Labour Union suggesting
that we work on the lines of the following recommendations:-

(1) That the idea of holding a demonstration parade be
abandoned because the Police will undoubtedly oppose it.
page_data.zh:
(11)

属于旧车厂的工人代表于12月11日举行会议，敦促罢工者保持坚定，战斗到底。其中一位发言人宣称：“如果外国鬼子打算放假一周，我们就再多停工十天。”这次会议的结果是成立了一个登记委员会来控制运动。罢工者被告知会有罢工救济金保障，并被告知不必为罢工担忧。“打倒叛徒蔣少山（Chiang Siao San）”的呼声到处高声响起。蔣少山是对罢工组织涣散负主要责任的人。我们控制罢工者的方法逐渐产生了有益的效果，此时的总体迹象对我们有利。

拟议中的登记委员会仍在组建过程中，12月12日设立了一个登记处。该处的成立取得了巨大成功。仅在这一天，就有不少于800名工人在该处登记。随后进行了挨家挨户的访问，我们保持高度警觉，充分利用这些访问机会。向他们灌输了斗争的真正意义，并敦促他们保持不动摇。

在罢工的这一阶段，我们的目标基于以下三点：-

(1) 利用登记制度在罢工者中进行宣传。

(2) 通过获得上海公共租界工部局的许可，开展针对公司的示威活动。

(3) 建立一个由21人组成的罢工委员会，其中旧车厂和新车厂各出8名工人，机械师代表5名。

同日，我们收到上海总工会常务委员会的来信，建议我们按照以下建议行事：-

(1) 放弃举行示威游行的想法，因为警方无疑会反对。

page_data.en:
(12)

(2) That members of the Shop-keepers Union be instructed
to get their employers' seals secretly chopped on a petition
to be addressed to the Shanghai Municipal Council to inter-
vene in the strike and to urge the Tramway Co to bring about
an early settlement.

(3) That a manifesto be issued in the name of the strikers
to be distributed to all shops in town.

(4) That effective measure be taken to conduct a vigorous
campaign amongst the strikers.

None of these suggestions, however, were put into practice.
Our comrades (communists) implicated in the strike acted in
such a cowardly manner and on seeing that that the strike
committee followed suit. If asked to approach the Council
regarding the petition for permission to hold demonstrations
the committee would say, "So you want us to enter the death
zone." When a meeting is held they would always remain
silent asking us to adopt suitable measures but behind our
backs they complain that we never hold mass meetings and
always decide things partially at minor meetings without
giving heed to what they have to say. Such was the pre-
dicament we were in at that time and it was an utter
impossibility to embark on any systematic movement. But
thanks to the inactivity of the management we were still
able to control the strikers by means of our effective
propaganda.

(To be continued)

(Sent in March 16, 1928, 2.45 a.m.).
page_data.zh:
(12)

(2) 指示店员公会成员秘密获取雇主印章，盖在给上海公共租界工部局的请愿书上，请求介入罢工，并敦促电车公司尽早达成和解。

(3) 以罢工者名义发布宣言，分发至市内所有商店。

(4) 采取有效措施，在罢工者中开展 vigorous（有力/激烈）的运动。

然而，这些建议均未付诸实施。卷入罢工的我们的同志（共产党员）表现得如此怯懦，看到这种情况，罢工委员会也随波逐流。当被要求就举行示威的许可申请接触工部局时，委员会会说：“所以你们是想让我们进入死亡地带。”开会时，他们总是保持沉默，要求我们采取适当措施，但在背后却抱怨我们从不举行群众大会，总是在小型会议上片面地决定事情，而不 heed（理会/重视）他们的意见。这就是我们当时所处的困境，根本不可能开展任何系统性的运动。但得益于管理层的无所作为，我们仍然能够通过有效的宣传来控制罢工者。

（未完待续）

（1928年3月16日凌晨2点45分呈送）。
